zyntschnur.text: Zyntschnur brings a sharp, complete game: matchup rating up among the very best, bravery close to the top, and a rhythm that never cools. The accuracy is near the top, so is the headshot share, and the lifetime board confirms the matchups. This one rests on an older, smaller opponent sample, so treat it as a sketch.

zyr0seunc.text: Zyr0sEUNC plays a full, balanced game: stands alongside the best tracked over nearly every count, a fast tempo, and unruffled as fights harden. The numbers keep up as the opposition strengthens. Its lifetime ledger matches the matchups, a clean agreement. A strong regular, through and through.

zyr0sncx.text: Zyr0sNCx plays a complete game: stands at the peak of the board across nearly every measure, a brisk rhythm, and resolute as fights harden. The numbers hold as the opposition strengthens. Its edge holds firm against the strongest third. The lifetime board paints the same picture as the matchups, a clean agreement.

zyr0s.text: Zyr0s has played since 2018 and still plays flat out: among the very best tracked, blazing tempo behind it, raising the output against stronger opposition. The matchup kill-death numbers sit near the top, and the strongest-third edge slips a touch. A veteran game, still at full speed.

zialvs.text: ZialVS plays a balanced, top-shelf game: sharp in the matchups, steady in the face of harder foes, with bravery near the top too, and accuracy sitting near the summit. Consistency is the lone mid-pack line on an otherwise upper-tier sheet. Both boards agree: a balanced card, end of story.

zaazaawuying.text: ZaaZaaWuYing is a young account carrying a truly complete game: top shelf in the matchups, and accuracy at the ceiling. The edge holds against the hardest third too, which is rare this early on. Early read, though the opening pages already carry some serious weight.

zthassassinsssssssssssssssssssss.text: zthAssassinsssssssssssssssssssss picks the moment, then ends it: bravery sits near the bottom, yet the matchup kill-death mark lands among the very best tracked, with resistance near the top. The pace is middling, accuracy below average, headshots nearly absent, and the lifetime IvI near the bottom — the matchups see a far deadlier game than the lifetime board does. Consistency trails below average, but the chosen fights are won decisively.

zoogie.text: Zoogie has been at it since 2013, and the card reads like a masterclass: matchup rating, activity, bravery, resistance, and matchup kill-death all sitting in the top ranks, with a pace to match. Precise aim, plenty of headshots, and the lifetime ledger tells the same story. Even against the strongest third, the game barely slips — a veteran who still sets the pace.

zewgie.text: Zewgie has been dueling since 2012, and the record is rich: the matchup kill-death mark hovers near the top, with rating, tempo, bravery, resistance — all holding in the upper tier. Accuracy sits above average, the headshot share top-shelf, while the lifetime IvI holds the upper tier too. Read this as a sketch, mind you — the opponent sample is older and smaller, leaving the edges soft.

zouiette.text: ZouIette builds wins on precision and poise: rating, tempo, bravery, resistance — the matchup kill-death line sits right beside it, with rating, tempo, bravery, resistance — every adjusted line in the upper tier. The headshot share is only middling, and the lifetime IvI rests mid-pack — the lifetime board undersells what the matchups prove. A steady, complete player whose best work shows up where it counts.

zzerocoollruss.text: ZzeroCoollRUSS plays a sharp, high-tempo game built on output near the top. The game keeps its edge as the opposition improves, with the matchup rating near the top, though the lifetime board sits a step below the matchups, and the consistency mark dips below average. Treat this one as a rough draft, not the finished work: the opponent sample behind it comes from an older, smaller pool.

zugie.text: Zugie has been winning since 2013: rating, activity, bravery and resistance all sit in the upper tier, kills arrive at a top rate, and the aim is sharp with headshots landing near the summit. The lifetime board agrees, full stop. The one soft spot is the toughest third, where the edge dips below average. A veteran who still plays the whole game at a high level.

zlaas.text: Zlaas plays a complete game at the highest level: activity, bravery, and resistance all sit near the very top, and the headshot share leads everyone tracked. The matchup kill-death mark sits well above average, and the consistency mark holds near the top, so the edge survives the strongest third. Even the lifetime numbers agree, sitting near the top alongside the matchups.

zygorg.text: Zygorg fights uphill and wins anyway: a top-tier matchup rating, bravery near the top, and resistance near the top. The lifetime kill-death line sits near the top while the head-to-head kill-death figure lands above average, and headshots land near the top as well. A strong, uphill game with the lifetime board backing up the matchups.

zugiee.text: Zugiee plays like a storm front: upper-tier rating, blistering tempo, and a dueling record that stays strong whoever steps up. Headshots land near the summit and the lifetime numbers back the matchups. Even against the hardest third the edge holds firm in the upper tier, so tougher lobbies change little. A complete, confident card from a young account.

zampharosite.text: zAmpharosite plays a patient, measured game: top-tier matchup rating, bravery that keeps pace as enemies toughen, and a duel record well above average. The lifetime ledger sits squarely in the middle, and the aim stays ordinary — the matchups are the louder half of the card. A steady riser whose best work shows up where the fights are hardest.

zoiberg125rus.text: Since 2018, Zoiberg125rus has held a top-tier matchup rating: bravery and resistance well above average, and a duel tally to match. The aim stays ordinary, the lifetime ledger rests in the middle, and consistency holds mid-pack. A veteran whose matchups run hotter than the career totals.

zyw0ooo.text: zyw0ooo arrived in 2025 and already plays like a storm: tempo, bravery, kill pace, output, and accuracy all near the summit, with lifetime IvI to match. The matchup grade runs well above average, with headshots sitting above average too. Consistency holds mid-pack — the single calm line in a card that never sits still.

zeethvs.text: zeethvs plays like a storm with the throttle pinned: tempo, bravery, and kill pace all sit near the very summit, while accuracy and headshots keep pace at the same altitude, and the lifetime board rides with them. The matchup rating sits well above average, and the faceoff kill-death count holds firm beside it. Only consistency dips below average against the strongest third, the one soft seam in a card built for speed. A relentless force who rarely slows down.

zleoon.text: zLeoon runs toward the hardest fights and usually comes out ahead: bravery near the top, a blistering kill pace, and a matchup rating comfortably above average. The aim is sharp and headshots land where they count. The one wrinkle: the toughest-third line falls below average, the only line that refuses to keep up with the rest.

zachhalo1.text: zachhalo1 is steady across the whole card: rating, tempo, bravery and resistance each above average, with the kill pace keeping step and the lifetime board close behind. Accuracy and headshots sit mid-pack, and consistency lands in the same middle ground. A veteran since 2014 who rarely has a bad line on the card.

zhubao3.text: zhubao3 plays a remarkably even game: every line on the card sits above the middle, from the matchup rating through activity, bravery, and resistance. The kill-death balance sheet in duels matches that picture, and the lifetime numbers agree across the board. Consistency sits mid-pack, the single ordinary line — a solid, unspectacular foundation.

zeylven.text: Zeylven is steady strength without a headline: the matchup rating runs well above average, with the pace and the bravery to match. The duel scorecard holds well above average, and the career numbers land mid-pack. The aim is mid-pack, the headshots ordinary, but the card holds together — a regular since 2022 who turns up and delivers.

zehpyrsis.text: zehpyrsis plays the most even card in the book: every line except one sits well above average, from matchup rating and tempo through bravery, resistance, and lifetime numbers. The lone exception is the edge against the toughest third, which lands mid-pack instead of climbing with the rest. No headline, no hole — just a complete regular who turns up ready every fight.

zergboom.text: ZergBoom arrived in 2025 with a remarkably sharp aim: accuracy sits near the very top, while rating, tempo, bravery, and resistance all clear the middle with room to spare. Against the strongest third the edge collapses, the one line that falls away from the rest. A fighter with a fine trigger and one hard lesson still ahead.

zalakazite.text: zAlakazite has no soft edge: above the middle on every matchup measure, from rating to bravery to resistance, and the head-to-head ledger stays green. The pace runs brisk and the aim sits in the middle, while the lifetime numbers land mid-pack too — a card with no holes in it. The kind of regular who makes every fight a grind for the other side.

z6i.text: Z6i wins more than the aim suggests: a good stride above the average, unhurried on the trigger, and level as the stakes climb. The headshots land where they count even while the accuracy sits below average. Lifetime board and matchups point the same way, which keeps the story honest: a strong regular with a sharp eye.

zynxao.text: ZynXao pairs a strong all-round card with a sharp finishing touch: above average across the matchups, brisk in tempo, and landing headshots at a top-tier rate. The lifetime IvI line sits top-tier too, so the two boards agree. A veteran since 2015, still sharp, still dangerous in any exchange.

zephixium.text: Zephixium has been at it since 2013, and the card still reads like a strong regular's. The adjusted marks hold well above average, the tempo stays quick, and the edge holds up under sterner pressure. The head-to-head figures rest mid-pack, the one ordinary note, while the lifetime board echoes the matchups. A steady hand who has never really slipped.

zuixktr.text: Zuixktr plays the longest game on the board: mid-pack on tempo, unhurried to the point of stillness, and patient when the duels turn hard. Head-to-head, the tally sits near the top, while the lifetime kill-death board ranks among the very best tracked — yet the pace stays near the bottom, and the accuracy too. A study in selectivity: few engagements, chosen carefully, and won far more often than not.

zless.text: zLess plays a brisk, accurate game: comfortably above the middle across the matchup board, sharp of aim, and unmoved as the opposition strengthens. The lifetime numbers edge a little hotter still, with the IvI line near the top, while the head-to-head kill-death record sits mid-pack. In the hardest fights the edge dips a touch, the one soft note. The opponent sample here is older and smaller, so read this as a sketch rather than a finished portrait.

zecurenc.text: ZecureNC plays at a tempo few can match: well above average overall, dashing through every exchange, and bolder than most as the enemies get stronger, and the pace rides near the very top. The aim is crisp, and the career ledger confirms the recent form. The matchup tally itself lands in the middle, the one calm corner of a loud game. A high-tempo regular who keeps the other side scrambling from the first shot to the last.

zurkoslat.text: Since 2013, Zurkoslat has been tough to break down: well above average overall, comfortable as the opposition strengthens, and unfazed when the opposition gets strongest, holding its shape against the toughest foes. The aim sits below the middle, and the long view undersells the whole picture. The direct duels lean their way more often than they don't. A veteran regular who keeps turning up and keeps coming out ahead.

zerwiny.text: zerwiny fights with a steady hand and a cool head: the output barely changes whether the opposition is soft or seasoned, and the exchange stays above the middle either way. Resistance is the quiet strength here, holding firm through the hardest stretches. A reliable, no-drama operator who gets the job done.

ziviz.text: Ziviz wins the long game: patient, unhurried, and hard to knock off balance, they come out ahead in most exchanges without ever looking rushed. Their resistance runs above the middle, and the duel outcomes follow the same upward line. Nothing here screams spectacle; this is a veteran who knows exactly which fights are worth taking.

zonafrancabcn.text: zonafrancaBCN has been fighting since 2016, and the matchup game sits well above average: careful, steady, and hard to shake. The lifetime IvI line runs near the bottom, and headshots stay rare, so the strength lives in the duels rather than the long view. A patient regular who keeps showing up and keeps the fight honest.

zipulh.text: Zipulh brings a busy, rugged game with an all-round showing well above average: a rolling tempo, and a matchup record above the middle. The aim wanders — accuracy sits below the middle — yet the results hold up, and the lifetime figures sit in the middle. Once the going gets hardest, that touch starts to thin, the single soft spot in a strong young game.

zurnt.text: Zurnt is the picture of a steady regular: well above average overall, hard to shift in a straight fight, with a matchup record sitting in the middle. The game holds its shape when the opposition strengthens, and the lifetime figures match the matchups stride for stride. Nothing flashy, just a reliable presence who makes every fight honest.
